evidence.note: Falsified assumption that `npm install` downloads deps (no internet) drove a real revision of the packaging approach: dependencies → peerDependencies + offline config + runtime symlinks. Approach-level rework, not just a patch.

When @vitejs/plugin-rsc demanded build.rollupOptions.input, the agent explicitly weighed 'configure environments properly OR implement our own SSR middleware' and pivoted to disabling serverHandler + own middleware. Deliberate — but a bypass of the RSC foundation rather than wiring it correctly, which undercuts later subsystems (use cache/RSC).

Long stretch of local fixes (symlinks, stderr pipe deadlock, ESM/CJS require, npx resolution) to the runtime node_modules foundation — repeated patching without revisiting whether the hand-written-dist + runtime-symlink foundation was sound.
Hydration handled as additive fixes (add client hydration, then improve it) rather than a foundational render-pipeline refactor.
Declares completion without ever confirming a passing test count (results file never produced); no re-verification of dependents after the pivots, so no coherent architecture is demonstrably reached.

reasoning: The agent twice revises an approach when reality contradicts it — the dependency/packaging scheme (91-127) and the RSC integration (133-143, with explicit weighing) — matching anchor 5's 'recognizes an approach is wrong and reworks that subsystem.' It falls short of 8 because the RSC pivot chooses a workaround that bypasses the foundation rather than correctly wiring it, much of the middle is undifferentiated local patching of the runtime-symlink foundation (151-213), and it never re-verifies dependents or reaches a green suite (263-267). Net behavior lands between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 5.
